title: Building a Better Station Food Culture
subtitle: Small changes that stick
description: How to build better fire station food culture: fair rotations, better groceries, rookie support, and meals that make cooking worth the effort.
intro: Better station food culture is not a wellness poster — it is fair labor, decent groceries, and meals people want to eat. Crews cook when cooking feels worth it: clear roles, reimbursement that works, and less public griping about the result.

sections.heading: Where to start
paragraphs: Fix cleanup fairness first. Then grocery splits. Then one recurring cook night with a reliable recipe.

sections.heading: Habits that compound
paragraphs: Stock basics, rotate cooks, and celebrate wins on the whiteboard. Culture shifts when cooking feels fair — not when someone gives a speech about wellness.

practicalAdvice: Rotate cooks weekly — visibility prevents burnout.
Stock the pantry with basics so dinner is not 'shop from zero.'
Celebrate good meals — photos on the board, not only complaints.

faqs.question: Where do these recipes come from?
faqs.answer: Each link goes to a full recipe on Firehall Meals — crew-sized portions, station timing, and steps written for a shared kitchen. Not home-blog scaling.

faqs.question: What if crew size or time changes tonight?
faqs.answer: Use Find a Meal with your headcount and minutes available. It pulls from the same hall-tested dinners these guides recommend.
